elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer for covered claims and losses.
elements.evidence: The Servicer indemnifies the Issuer for enumerated fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer's affiliates for covered claims and losses.
elements.evidence: The clause covers named trustees and the named parties' officers, directors, employees and agents, but does not cover the Issuer's affiliates as a class.

elements.element: Vendor has an affirmative duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: The clause reimburses amounts incurred by Indemnified Persons in defending themselves, but does not require the Servicer to undertake or provide the defense.

elements.element: The indemnity covers third-party claims arising from the specified indemnity triggers.
elements.evidence: The indemnity broadly covers all claims, actions and suits resulting from triggers (A)-(D), and trigger (D) expressly refers to third-party claims.

elements.element: The IP indemnity covers third-party claims alleging that the services, including systems, software or processes used to perform them, infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Trigger (D) covers any third-party claim that a system, software or process used by the Servicer to perform its servicing obligations infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The IP indemnity covers third-party claims alleging that deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Trigger (D) covers systems, software and processes used by the Servicer, but does not expressly cover deliverables furnished to the Customer.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and covered beneficiaries for claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Trigger (B) expressly covers losses resulting from the Servicer's breach of applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and covered beneficiaries for a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Trigger (C) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Obligor data or other confidential information caused by the Servicer.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and covered beneficiaries for claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Trigger (A) covers the Servicer's willful misconduct and gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonably prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: No claim-notice requirement appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure addresses which party controls the defense and settlement of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no defense-control or settlement-control provision.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation in defending an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, with no other Customer indemnity triggers.
elements.evidence: The provided operative clause imposes no indemnity obligation on the Issuer or other Customer-side party, so the condition requiring restriction of any such indemnity is demonstrably absent in this clause.

elements.element: Vendor provides an IP indemnity covering third-party infringement or misappropriation claims arising from Vendor's performance.
elements.evidence: Trigger (D) expressly indemnifies against third-party claims that systems, software or processes used by the Servicer infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by the Customer or another non-Vendor party appears.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes claims arising from Customer-provided specifications or instructions.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification or instruction exclusion appears.

elements.element: For covered IP claims, Vendor must procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No obligation to procure continued use rights appears.

elements.element: For covered IP claims, Vendor must modify the affected services or deliverables to make them non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears.

elements.element: For covered IP claims, Vendor must replace the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing equivalents.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears.

elements.element: If the other IP remedies are unavailable, Vendor must provide an appropriate refund.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy or remedy hierarchy appears.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability is subject to a separate super-cap.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no liability cap applicable to the Servicer's indemnity obligations.

elements.element: The indemnity super-cap equals three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No three-times-annual-fees cap is stated. The non-operative margin comment cannot supply or alter a cap.

result.reason: The redline cleanly adds breach-of-law, Vendor-caused data incident and third-party IP heads while retaining the existing misconduct indemnity. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits affiliates as a beneficiary class, an affirmative defense duty, deliverables-based IP coverage, and all notice, defense-control and cooperation procedures. It also does not reach the fallback because none of the usual IP exclusions, infringement remedies or the 3× annual-fees super-cap is operative. The changes preserve the existing unrelated terms and introduce no evident contradiction, but they are incomplete for either required level; the margin comment has no operative effect.
